title: 2019 AMC 10A Problem 13
statement: Let \(\triangle ABC\) be an isosceles triangle with \(BC = AC\) and \(\angle ACB = 40^{\circ}.\) Construct the circle with diameter \(\overline{BC},\) and let \(D\) and \(E\) be the other intersection points of the circle with the sides \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{AB},\) respectively. Let \(F\) be the intersection of the diagonals of the quadrilateral \(BCDE.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle BFC ?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(\overline{BC}\) is the diameter of the circle, we get that \(\angle BDC\) and \(\angle BEC\) are right angles.

We know that \(\angle ABC = 70^{\circ}\) from the fact that \(\triangle ABC\) is isosceles.

In \(\triangle BCE\) and \(\triangle BCD\), respectively, \[ \begin{aligned} \angle ECB&=180^{\circ}-70^{\circ}-90^{\circ}\\ &=20^{\circ} \end{aligned} \] and \[ \begin{aligned} \angle DBC&=180^{\circ}-40^{\circ}-90^{\circ}\\ &=50^{\circ}. \end{aligned} \]

Because \(F\) lies on \(BD\) and \(CE\), the other two angles of \(\triangle BFC\) are \(50^{\circ}\) and \(20^{\circ}\). Hence \[ \begin{aligned} \angle BFC&=180^{\circ}-50^{\circ}-20^{\circ}\\ &=110^{\circ}. \end{aligned} \] Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Angles subtended by a diameter are right angles
Use the isosceles angles of \(\triangle ABC\) to chase the remaining angles
